input.summary:
I found no linearizability violation in target-a, so I can't claim a bug. I ran 17 experiments, all with verdict ok. They covered these cases:
- Leader isolated, and leader in a minority partition, with reads sent to the leader and to any node.
- Leader and follower pauses, including a zombie leader resuming after a new election.
- Crashes and restarts of the leader, of followers, and of a majority at once, plus crashes during elections.
- Flapping partitions and rolling single-node isolations over 8 s.
- Drops up to 15%, duplicates up to 40%, and latencies up to 150 ms.
- High read ratio on a single key, and several seeds (42, 7, 5, 3, 11, 21, 99).
Stale reads from deposed leaders, lost acknowledged writes and duplicate application were all absent from the histories. The checker never reported a violation, and none of the runs came back "unknown". The cluster looks correct, or its bug needs a narrower trigger than I tried.
